title: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)

sections.label: Full-day preschool places increase
sections.summary: Full-day preschool places rose from around 120,000 in 2015 to around 220,000, and the 80% Government-supported preschool commitment will be met by end-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2015, we had around 120,000 full-day preschool places.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We worked hard to increase this number and today, we have around 220,000 full-day preschool places, enough to accommodate every resident child aged three and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: During the 2019 National Day Rally, then-Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong announced our commitment to provide places for 80% of preschoolers in a Government-supported preschool.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: I am glad to share that by the end of 2025, we will meet this commitment.

sections.label: ECDA adding preschool places
sections.summary: From 2025 to 2029, ECDA will work with Anchor Operators to add almost 40,000 full-day preschool places, about 6,000 for infants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: From 2025 to 2029, the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) will work with Anchor Operators (AOP) to add almost 40,000 full-day preschool places, of which about 6,000 will cater to infants.

sections.label: 2026 full-day childcare fees
sections.summary: In 2026, full-day childcare fees will be $610 for AOP and $650 for POP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: What this means is that, in 2026, full-day childcare fees will be $610 for AOP and $650 for POP.

sections.label: Subsidised fees for dual income family
sections.summary: In 2026, a dual income family earning $10,000 monthly will pay $235 per month for full-day childcare in an AOP preschool after subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2026, a dual income family with monthly income of $10,000 will pay $235 per month for full-day childcare in an AOP preschool after subsidies, half of what they would have paid in 2019.

sections.label: Parenting resources and FFL expansion
sections.summary: The Parenting for Wellness toolbox provides resources on deepening parent-child relationships, and FFL@Community will expand to all towns nationwide by end-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Parenting for Wellness toolbox provides resources on how to deepen parent-child relationships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will expand FFL@Community to all towns nationwide by end-2025.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant increase
sections.summary: The Home Caregiving Grant was doubled from $200 to up to $400 a month in 2023 and will increase to up to $600 a month from April 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We enhanced the Home Caregiving Grant in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We doubled the amount from $200 to up to $400 a month in 2023; and in this Budget, the Home Caregiving Grant will be further increased to up to $600 a month, from April 2026.

sections.label: Shared Parental Leave scheme
sections.summary: Eligible parents can receive an additional six weeks of paid parental leave shared between both parents from 1 April 2025, rising to 10 weeks in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The upcoming Shared Parental Leave scheme will allow eligible parents to receive an additional six weeks of paid parental leave to be shared between both parents from 1 April 2025 and this will be increased to 10 weeks in 2026.

sections.label: Support for single unwed mothers
sections.summary: Child development benefits go to all families regardless of marital status, and single unwed mothers facing financial difficulties get support through KidSTART, ComLink+ and rental housing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Benefits supporting the growth and development of children are given to all families, regardless of the parents' marital status.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For single unwed mothers facing financial difficulties, support comes through other forms, such as through KidSTART, ComLink+ and also access to rental housing, if that is what they are applying for.

sections.label: Large Families Scheme
sections.summary: The Large Families Scheme will further defray costs for families with three or more children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Through the Large Families Scheme, we will further defray costs for families with three or more children.

sections.label: CDA for preschool incidental costs
sections.summary: From May 2025, parents can use the CDA for all incidental costs at approved preschools registered under the CDA scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: From May 2025, parents can use the CDA for all incidental costs at approved preschools registered under the CDA scheme.

sections.label: CDA Government funding amounts
sections.summary: Depending on birth order, families who save up to the co-matching cap can tap Government funding of between $9,000 and $20,000 in their children's CDA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Depending on the child's birth order, families who save up to the co-matching cap will be able to tap on Government funding of between $9,000 and $20,000 in their children's CDA.

sections.label: CPF top-up matching for disabilities
sections.summary: The Government will match every dollar of CPF top-ups received by eligible persons with disabilities, up to an annual cap of $2,000 and a lifetime limit of $20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Government will match every dollar of Central Provident Fund (CPF) top-ups received by eligible persons with disabilities, up to an annual cap of $2,000 and a lifetime limit of $20,000.

sections.label: SNTC caregiver top-up matching grant
sections.summary: A matching grant of up to $10,000 will be provided for eligible caregivers' top-ups to SNTC trust accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister announced in the Budget speech, we will provide a matching grant of up to $10,000 for top-ups by eligible caregivers to SNTC trust accounts.

sections.label: Preschool places, fees and CDA
sections.summary: It sets out preschool place targets, fee cap reductions, expanded CDA use for incidental fees, and the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2019, we provided Government-supported preschool places for 50% of preschoolers, and by the end of 2025, we will be able to provide Government-supported preschool places for 80% of preschoolers, fulfilling our promise made at the National Day Rally 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will continue our efforts, adding almost 40,000 more full-day preschool places from 2025 to 2029, including around 6,000 infant care places.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2023, monthly fee caps were reduced by $40, with another $40 reduction in early 2025, and a further $30 reduction in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To ensure families can afford preschool care and education and to help families in need, we will expand the use of CDA to allow parents to use their CDA to pay for preschool incidental fees at all preschools registered under the CDA scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For example, we introduced the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme, where parents can top-up money into the CPF account of their child with special needs, and the Government will match every dollar deposited, up to a lifetime cap of $20,000.

sections.label: ComCare cash rates enhancement
sections.summary: ComCare Short- to-Medium Term and Long Term Assistance cash rates will be increased to support basic needs, alongside regular quantum review.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Recently, studies from the Singapore Management University (SMU) and the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) found that Singapore residents view social activities and the ability to manage minor exigencies as basic needs that the Government and community could share responsibility in providing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: That is why, as Prime Minister Wong mentioned in his Budget speech, we will now enhance our social safety net by increasing ComCare Short- to-Medium Term Assistance and Long Term Assistance cash rates to support these needs, alongside our regular review of the ComCare quantum.

sections.label: ComLink+ families in rental housing
sections.summary: ComLink+ is now supporting around 10,000 families living in public rental housing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: ComLink+ is now supporting around 10,000 families living in public rental housing.

sections.label: ComLink+ packages and family coaches
sections.summary: Close to 1,600 families are on the packages, and there are 260 family coaches, targeting 300 by mid-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Close to 1,600 families have been emplaced on either or both of these packages.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To power ComLink+, we need a strong team of committed and professional officers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We now have 260 family coaches and are on track to reach our target of 300 by mid-2025.

sections.label: Trial for ComLink+ health needs
sections.summary: A new model of support to address the health needs of ComLink+ families is being trialled later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To this end, we are trialling a new model of support to address the health needs of ComLink+ families later this year.

sections.label: HDB ComLink+ home ownership
sections.summary: HDB is partnered to give ComLink+ families home ownership planning and guidance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: First, we are partnering the Housing and Development Board (HDB) to provide ComLink+ families with home ownership planning and guidance.

sections.label: ComLink+ flat purchase and grant
sections.summary: Eligible first-time ComLink+ rental families can buy shorter-lease flats, and the Fresh Start Housing Grant rises from $50,000 to $75,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As Minister of State Faishal has shared, eligible first-time ComLink+ families in public rental housing will be able to buy shorter-lease flats alongside Second-Timer families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The Fresh Start Housing Grant for eligible second-timers will also be increased from $50,000 to $75,000.

sections.label: Family Services Review Committee convened
sections.summary: In June 2024, MSF convened the Family Services Review Committee.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In June 2024, MSF convened the Family Services Review Committee.

sections.label: Committee and Working Group representatives
sections.summary: Fifty representatives from 28 social service agencies and associations are involved across the Committee and Working Groups.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Fifty representatives from 28 social service agencies and associations are involved across the Committee and Working Groups.

sections.label: PwD employment rate and ITE support
sections.summary: PwD employment rose to 33.6% in 2023 to 2024, and ITE and SG Enable's programme will be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The employment rate of PwDs aged between 15 and 64 has increased, from 28.2% in 2019 to 2020, to 33.6% in 2023 to 2024, and we will continue to push towards our goal of 40% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We thank Ms Denise Phua and Mr Ong Hua Han for their queries in this area.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) and SG Enable's internship and employment support programme will be enhanced to provide further employment support to more students with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This includes pre-employment training, career exploration and post-graduation job placement with up to one year of on-site support.

sections.label: Enabling Employment Credit extension
sections.summary: The Enabling Employment Credit will be extended till end-2028 to support employment of PwDs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As shared at MOM's Committee of Supply debate, the Enabling Employment Credit will be extended till end-2028 to support the employment of PwDs.

sections.label: Enabling Skills for Life Programme
sections.summary: The Enabling Skills for Life Programme Proof-of-Concept will be launched from 2025 to 2028 to support PwDs in lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: These programmes can be organised more conveniently and provide opportunities to build up skills for independence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Therefore, the new Enabling Skills for Life Programme Proof-of-Concept will be launched from 2025 to 2028, to support PwDs in lifelong learning.

sections.label: Home Support Programme launch
sections.summary: The Home Support Programme will launch in 2026 to support PwDs with low to moderate needs to live at home as long as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To plug this gap, we will launch the Home Support Programme in 2026, to support PwDs with low to moderate needs to live at home as long as possible.

sections.label: Enabled Living Programme pilot
sections.summary: The Enabled Living Programme will be piloted in the second half of this year to help them continue living in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For them, we will pilot the Enabled Living Programme in the second half of this year to help them continue living in the community.

sections.label: New assessment centres
sections.summary: From 2026 onwards, PwDs can enjoy shorter waiting times for an appointment with two new assessment centres supported by SG Enable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: From 2026 onwards, PwDs can enjoy shorter waiting times for an appointment with the launch of two new assessment centres supported by SG Enable.

sections.label: Higher income qualifying threshold
sections.summary: The maximum qualifying per capita household income for those services and the Assistive Technology Fund will be raised to $4,800 from next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Mr Ong Hua Han will be glad that we are raising the maximum qualifying per capita household income for those services and the Assistive Technology Fund to $4,800, from next year.

sections.label: Employment strategy key areas
sections.summary: The employment strategy will focus on six key areas and support businesses through legal protections, wage offsets, workplace modifications, capability building and recognition frameworks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Our employment strategy will focus on six key areas and support businesses through various means, including legal protections, wage offsets, workplace modifications, capability building and recognition frameworks.

sections.label: Nurturing families core principles
sections.summary: Efforts to nurture strong families, resilient individuals and a caring society rest on three core principles: family-centricity, a strengths-based approach, and proactive upstream engagement and intervention.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Over the recent years, we have made significant strides in nurturing strong families, resilient individuals and a caring society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: These efforts have been undergirded by three core principles: family-centricity, strengths-based approach to uplift the family and proactive, upstream engagement and intervention.

sections.label: ComLink+ family coach partnership
sections.summary: Under ComLink+, a dedicated family coach partners the family, helping them stay focused on their goals and work towards lasting change.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Under ComLink+, for example, a dedicated family coach partners the family, helping them to stay focused on their goals and work towards lasting change.

sections.label: KidSTART equips families early
sections.summary: KidSTART is cited as an example of equipping families as early as the point of pregnancy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: KidSTART is a good example of how we equip families as early as the point of pregnancy.

sections.label: NCSS role as sector developer
sections.summary: NCSS has transformed beyond a membership body to a sector developer, and amendments to the NCSS Act will reflect and strengthen this role.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: At the sector level, National Council of Social Service (NCSS) has transformed itself beyond being a membership body, to deliver stronger outcomes for social service users as a sector developer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We have been engaging the sector and will introduce amendments to the NCSS Act to reflect and strengthen NCSS’ role as a sector developer.

sections.label: grovve integrated mental wellness centre
sections.summary: NCSS and the Institute of Mental Health are bringing together 12 partners to co-locate services at an integrated mental wellness centre called grovve, to be launched later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To share one such initiative, NCSS, together with the Institute of Mental Health, is bringing together 12 partners to co-locate services at an integrated mental wellness centre called "grovve". "grovve" will be officially launched later this year.

sections.label: Social Residential Homes Bill licensing
sections.summary: MSF has introduced the Social Residential Homes Bill, which codifies sector progress through a new licensing regime with requirements for client safety and wellness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To Mr Baey Yam Keng’s question, I am pleased to share that MSF has introduced the Social Residential Homes Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, we will codify the good progress made by the sector through a new licensing regime, with clear requirements to ensure the safety and wellness of clients.

sections.label: Centre for Evidence set up
sections.summary: NCSS and Tote Board set up the Centre for Evidence in 2024 to propagate the Sector Evaluation Framework and partner SSAs on programme evaluation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In addition, NCSS, in collaboration with Tote Board, set up the Centre for Evidence in 2024 to propagate the Sector Evaluation Framework and partner SSAs to strengthen programme evaluation.

sections.label: Sustainable Philanthropy Framework adoption
sections.summary: Over 40 businesses adopted the Sustainable Philanthropy Framework to measure social impact, and more employers are joining SGSHARE through ComChest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since we launched the Sustainable Philanthropy Framework last year, more than 40 businesses have adopted the framework to measure their social impact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In addition, more employers are coming onboard SGSHARE, which allows employees to donate a small amount of their salary each month, through ComChest.

sections.label: SG Gives matching grant launch
sections.summary: As part of SG60, the Government will launch a $250 million SG Gives matching grant to match donations through Community Chest, President's Challenge and Collective for a Stronger Society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As shared by Prime Minister in the Budget Speech, as part of SG60, the Government will launch a $250 million SG Gives matching grant to match donations made through Community Chest, President’s Challenge and Collective for a Stronger Society.

sections.label: SG Gives donor commitments
sections.summary: Details will be shared later, and PropNex and the Rao Family Foundation have each committed to contribute for SG Gives in commemoration of SG60.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will share more details in due course.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am also heartened that since the announcement at Budget, PropNex, a local-listed real estate company has committed to contribute more than $1 million over three years for SG Gives in commemoration of SG60.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Rao Family Foundation, too, has come forward and will contribute $1 million over three years.

sections.label: SSAs salary guideline adherence
sections.summary: Today, about 80% of SSAs adhere to the salary guidelines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Today, about 80% of SSAs adhere to the salary guidelines.

sections.label: Sector Awards for social service
sections.summary: The new Sector Awards for Social Service Professionals were launched, including the President's Awards for Social Service Professionals as the sector's pinnacle award.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To do this, we recently launched the new Sector Awards for Social Service Professionals, including the new President’s Awards for Social Service Professionals, which will be the pinnacle award for the sector.

sections.label: Family support principles
sections.summary: The Government will continue strengthening efforts based on three key principles, the first two being family-centred policies and proactive support for families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Government will continue to strengthen our efforts based on three key principles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: First, we will strengthen our policies to be family-centred, and to support all families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Second, we will support families in a proactive way.

sections.label: Strengths-based family support
sections.summary: The third principle is taking a strengths-based approach to supporting families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Third, we will take a strengths-based approach to supporting families.

sections.label: Year of Celebrating Social Service Professionals
sections.summary: 2025 has been dedicated as the Year of Celebrating Social Service Professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As such, we have dedicated 2025 as the Year of Celebrating Social Service Professionals.

sections.label: ECDA manpower and perception surveys
sections.summary: ECDA's 2021 manpower study and 2023 perception survey found educators' main concerns were poor work-life balance, excessive administrative duties and demanding parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Maybe I will handle the second question first, because the Member has mentioned this several times already.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, first and foremost, ECDA undertakes several surveys to understand the manpower issues in the sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, one of the surveys is a manpower study in 2021 and there is a perception survey conducted in 2023, and in both surveys, the main concerns expressed by educators were poor work-life balance, excessive administrative duties and also dealing with demanding parents.

sections.label: Preschool educator numbers and well-being
sections.summary: Preschool educators rose from over 18,000 in 2018 to 25,000 this year, and Teachers Day and Children's Day became preschool holidays from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And I had earlier shared that, in particular, we are expanding it in places where it is Government-supported.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, in terms of our number of preschool educators, we had over 18,000 preschool educators in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We have increased that to 25,000 this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: At the same time, we are also ensuring that we take into account their feedback on their well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: That is why we have designated Teachers Day, Children's Day as preschool holidays from 2024.

sections.label: Employer Development Grant for inclusive hiring
sections.summary: The Employer Development Grant was launched late last year to grow inclusive hiring and employment practices from within companies, alongside job coaching measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Last year, late last year, October, I believe, we launched the Employer Development Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: That really seeks to grow the culture of inclusion from within the organisation, because often times we can say that we want to show companies how to be inclusive from external.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: And that is why we have embarked on that journey to really grow inclusive hiring and inclusive employment practices from within each company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: And coupled with that, other measures that I have mentioned in my main speech which I will not belabour the points of – about job coaching, having those support become more intensive, and also, as I mentioned in response to Ms Denise Phua earlier, about having the job coach duration be longer than its previous usual one year tenure.

sections.label: Sheltered workshops and day activity centres
sections.summary: The Member asks how many have participated in sheltered workshops and day activity centres and their progress and outlook.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, on that note, I would like to ask Senior Parliamentary Secretary because he talked about sheltered workshops and day activity centres for those with higher support needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I just want to know how many have participated in these centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Number two, what is the progress and outlook of these centres, knowing that they are catering to higher needs, and it is not so porous, not so easy to progress.

sections.label: Rental flats and Charity Food Workgroup
sections.summary: The Member notes residents in rental flats get much help and alludes to the Charity Food Workgroup.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: For instance, in rental flats, the Member mentioned the word "pounce" in a positive way, that residents tended to get pounced upon, because of all the different types and sources of help that go to rental flat residents, perhaps also at specific intervals or times of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: This alludes to also another piece of work that I do in the Ministry and that is the Charity Food Workgroup.

sections.label: Disability spectrum and service pilots
sections.summary: The Member says each disability has a wide spectrum of needs, and many pilots address this sector's challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Even within each disability, there is a wide spectrum as to what the needs are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: So, in terms of what services should be planned and designed for each of these groups, I think the number of pilots and the number of things that we are doing now speaks to the exact challenge of this specific sector, which is why we have so many things that I have announced – the Home Support Programme, the Enabled Living Programme and so on and so forth.

sections.label: MSF longitudinal studies and GUSTO
sections.summary: The Member asks whether MSF commissions longitudinal studies for complex cases like the GUSTO study, and asks about a new development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: The question is, does MSF commission longitudinal studies, especially for intervention for complex cases, much like the way the GUSTO study is done by the Ministry of Health (MOH) and NUS, which is a very good study that even got featured in the Netflix documentary on neuroscience and the development of babies' brains, as well as, I understand, informed the design of KidSTART programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: So, my question is, is there a longitudinal study like this done in MSF?

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: My second question is on the new development "groove".

sections.label: ComCare review and longitudinal study MOUs
sections.summary: The Member says MSF worked with SMU and IPS on essential household needs, leading to the ComCare review, and signed MOUs including with SUSS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The first one, you may have heard in my speech, we worked with SMU and IPS and we established the essential household needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: And then MSF accepted it and therefore the ComCare review was made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We believe in evidence-based approaches and therefore, we have signed several memoranda of understanding (MOUs), one with the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) to undertake a major initiative on the longitudinal studies.

sections.label: NUS-IPS household study
sections.summary: The Member cites an NUS-IPS study on priorities and outcomes of 5,000 households across areas like employment and family support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Another example would be NUS-IPS study on the priorities and outcomes of 5,000 households in Singapore, across the diverse range of areas like employment, family support, young children's development.

sections.label: Caregiving Grant disbursement and donation
sections.summary: A Member thanks the Stephen Riady Foundation for a $1 million donation and asks if the Ministry will let care recipients nominate caregivers to receive Home Caregiving Grant funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: At the same time, I am also thankful to Stephen Riady Foundation for the $1 million donation to support this venture and to establish ourselves as a centre of learning, centre of social service development in our institutes of higher learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For Minister of State Sun, regarding the doubling of the Home Caregiving Grant over the years, I am very appreciative, but I also want to point out that many of the caregivers feel that this money is given into their mom or dad's account, and they do not feel like they should be taking their parents' money.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, will the Ministry look into adapting the disbursement process to put in a channel for care recipients to nominate the people or caregivers they would like these funds to be dispersed to?

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant payment
sections.summary: The Home Caregiving Grant is given to the care recipient but can go to a caregiver account the care recipient designates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
sentences.text: I will take the first question from the Member, Ms Carrie Tan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
sentences.text: So, the Home Caregiving Grant is given to the care recipient, but it can go to a caregiver account designated by the care recipient.

sections.label: Inclusive Business Programme support
sections.summary: Businesses hiring at least 20% persons with disabilities can be allocated HDB shop spaces, and SG Enable supports job redesign and employer training with grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
sentences.text: Under the Inclusive Business Programme, businesses that commit to having at least 20% of the hired workforce made up of PwDs actually can be directly allocated HDB shop spaces, for instance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
sentences.text: And beyond the Open Door programme, SG Enable also actively supports businesses in job redesign, employer training; there are grants available for companies and these grants can be tapped on.

sections.label: Public Education Standing Committee
sections.summary: The Member has raised previous Parliamentary Questions on this topic, and the Public Education Standing Committee was established in 2024 for a more inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
sentences.text: I think she has also raised previous Parliamentary Questions on this topic before.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
sentences.text: We agree with the Member that greater awareness, appreciation and understanding are definitely needed for a more inclusive society and to bolster these efforts, we established the Public Education Standing Committee in 2024.

sections.label: Whistle-blowing policies and NCSS
sections.summary: Every organisation should have whistle-blowing policies, and NCSS receives feedback from SSAs and will follow up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Because for whistle-blowing, every organisation should have policies on whistle-blowing and from time to time, NCSS does receive this feedback from the SSAs and we will follow up.

sections.label: Motion to reduce Estimates
sections.summary: A motion is moved that the total sum allocated for Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sections.label: Encouraging philanthropy beyond monetary donations
sections.summary: It asks how to encourage philanthropy in all forms beyond monetary donations, alongside $600 million set aside by the Government and Tote Board to match donations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In addition to the $600 million that will be set aside by the Government and the Tote Board to match donations made to charities and social causes in an effort to encourage philanthropy, how can we do more to encourage philanthropy in all forms, beyond just monetary donations?

sections.label: Early childhood curriculum standards frameworks
sections.summary: ECDA has the Early Years Development Framework guiding educators working with children from birth to three years old, and both frameworks were recently revised in 2023 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: On curriculum standards, the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) has the Early Years Development Framework, which guides early childhood educators working with children from birth to three years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Both frameworks have also been recently revised, in 2023 and 2022 respectively.

sections.label: Shortage and retention of early childhood educators
sections.summary: The sector faces a shortage of qualified educators and persistent retention issues, and it asks whether there are plans to increase investment in educators' professional development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, the sector still faces challenges in becoming an industry of choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: There remains a shortage of qualified educators willing to enter the field and retention is a persistent issue, with many educators leaving within the first few years of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Are there any plans to further increase our investments in the professional development of our early childhood educators?

sections.label: Value of informal care for seniors
sections.summary: A Duke-NUS Medical School study estimates informal care for seniors aged 75 and above at $1.28 billion annually, 11% of Government healthcare expenditure, and the Home Caregiving Grant is being increased to up to $600 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The total value of informal care for seniors aged 75 and above is estimated at $1.28 billion annually, equivalent to 11% of Government healthcare expenditure, according to a study by researchers from Duke-NUS Medical School.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I appreciate that the Home Caregiving Grant is being increased to up to $600 per month.

sections.label: Tiered caregiver payment proposal
sections.summary: It proposes a tiered caregiver payment for those who reduce work hours or leave employment to care for a family member, meeting a minimum caregiving threshold, with CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To put this into action, I propose a tiered caregiver payment for those who reduce their work hours or leave employment to care for a family member, provided they meet the minimum caregiving threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They should also receive Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions to safeguard their long-term financial security.

sections.label: Fairness for single unwed parents
sections.summary: It asks not for single unweds to be given more but for fairness, requesting the cash component of the Baby Bonus, the Parenthood Tax Rebate and the Working Mother's Child Relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am not asking for single unweds to be given more, but for it to be fair.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am asking for them to be given the cash component of the Baby Bonus, the Parenthood Tax Rebate and the Working Mother's Child Relief.

sections.label: Social worker funding and caseload
sections.summary: Social workers need MSF to review family service centre funding, provide more headcount funding and cap caseloads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The reality is that social workers are passionate about helping others, but they, too, need help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: They need MSF to help them do a deep review of the funding model of the family service centres, provide more funding for headcount and introduce a cap on the number of cases a social worker can handle.

sections.label: CPO caseload cap request
sections.summary: CPOs handle about 40 cases, which Eric Chua called too high, and the speaker hopes MSF will cap each CPO's cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Our CPOs handle about 40 cases at any point in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: As Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua shared: "I also think that 40 is a little bit too high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: We are trying to bring the number for the caseload down." CPOs are superheroes but they have a limit, and I know many are way past that limit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I hope MSF will help our CPOs and ensure that there is a cap on the number of cases each CPO can handle.

sections.label: ComCare healthy food assistance
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MSF will add ComCare in-kind healthy food and collaborate with MOH and HPB.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can I ask MSF if: one, will MSF consider adding a layer of ComCare in-kind assistance to provide a monthly supply of healthy food items curated with MOH's Health Promotion Board (HPB)?

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can MSF and MOH collaborate to enable healthier food for our lower-income Singaporeans on ComCare?

sections.label: ComLink+ preschool participation rate
sections.summary: An MSF November 2024 report found only 26% of ComLink+ families send children to preschool regularly, and MSF's plan is asked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: According to the Supporting Lower-Income Households trends report released by MSF in November 2024, only 26% of families on the ComLink+ scheme send their children to preschool regularly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: What is MSF's plan to improve the preschool participation rate for these families?

sections.label: ComLink+ Progress packages update
sections.summary: The speaker asks for an update on ComLink+ Progress packages covering preschool education, employment, financial stability and home ownership saving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: On that note, can the Ministry provide an update on the progress and achievements of ComLink+, including the rollout of ComLink+ Progress packages?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Chairman, the ComLink+ Progress packages aim to support the efforts of eligible lower-income families with young children to help them achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The packages focus on the four areas of preschool education, stable employment, improving financial stability through debt clearance and saving for home ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The package on preschool education was launched in August last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MSF announced that it was working towards launching the other three packages for employment, financial stability and saving for home ownership from this year, 2025.

sections.label: Continuum of support initiatives
sections.summary: The speaker says a continuum across living, learning and working is needed and welcomes the Enabling Services Hub, Enabling Business Hub and Enabled Living Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The solution lies in creating a continuum of support models across living, learning and working – three key pillars of life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am pleased that the Ministry has introduced three key initiatives: the Enabling Services Hub, the Enabling Business Hub and the Enabled Living Programme.

sections.label: SPED students stop learning
sections.summary: Many Government-funded SPED students stop learning after leaving school, largely due to the cliff effect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: While this is understandable, the reality is that many Government-funded Special Education (SPED) students stop learning altogether after leaving school, largely due to that proverbial "cliff effect".

sections.label: Study and top-up funding
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to commission a study on the cliff effect and consider top-up funding for adult learners with special educational needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Lifelong learning, therefore, is not a luxury, but a necessity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to commission a comprehensive study to address this "cliff effect" and consider adopting a top-up funding model for adult learners with special educational needs, closer to the support that they receive pre-age 18.

sections.label: Job Placement and Job Support
sections.summary: The current Job Placement and Job Support Programme provides support for only one year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The current Job Placement and Job Support Programme provides support for only one year.

sections.label: PwD employment barriers and target
sections.summary: Many persons with disabilities face barriers to jobs, and the Enabling Masterplan targets a 40% employment rate for PwDs by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Yet many persons with disabilities in Singapore continue to face significant barriers to securing jobs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Enabling Masterplan sets an ambitious and necessary target – a 40% employment rate for PwDs by 2030, for which I am very, very grateful.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: It demands concrete action to remove barriers, equip individuals and foster inclusive workplace cultures.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: With just five years remaining, what is MSF's strategy to accelerate inclusive employment and ensure that opportunities for PwDs are not just available, but actively created to meet this goal?

sections.label: MSF inclusive hiring plans
sections.summary: With five years left to meet the 40% employment target, the speaker asks whether MSF will share plans to accelerate inclusive hiring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With five years left to meet the Enabling Masterplan 2030 target of 40% employment, can MSF share its plans to bring to life strategies that encourage and accelerate inclusive hiring?

sections.label: Long-term care subsidy threshold
sections.summary: The monthly per capita household income threshold for long-term care subsidies and grants will increase to $4,800 from 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, the monthly per capita household income (PCHI) threshold for long-term care subsidies and grants are set to be increased to a standardised level of $4,800 from 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to Singapore Departmant of Statistics, median monthly PCHI has increased from $3,500 in 2023 to around $3,600 in 2024.

sections.label: National surveys on neurodivergence
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether it can conduct periodic national surveys on neurodivergence prevalence and challenges among adults.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry conduct periodic national surveys to gauge the prevalence of neurodivergence in our adult population and the challenges faced by neurodivergent adults?

sections.label: Inclusive society for neurodivergent individuals
sections.summary: The passage calls for an inclusive society and for support for neurodivergent individuals to extend beyond school into later life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the end of the day, this is about creating an inclusive society, one that recognises and values the contributions of all individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us ensure that support for neurodivergent individuals does not stop at the school gates but extends into the later stages of life.

sections.label: National framework for disability representation
sections.summary: MSF is urged to partner MDDI on a national framework, referencing New Zealand's Inclusive Code, for disability representation in advertising.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is a tool for advertising industry professionals to reflect on normalised but exclusionary practices, designed by disabled experts to help people design marketing campaigns that better include disabled people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I urge MSF to partner MDDI to establish a national framework, taking reference from New Zealand's Inclusive Code, to propel advertisers and content creators to incorporate intentional disability representation.

sections.label: Expanding Open Door Programme reach
sections.summary: The passage notes the Open Door Programme helps employers hire, train and integrate PWSNs, but says its reach needs expanding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While I am heartened by the Open Door Programme which encourages employers to hire, train and integrate PWSNs through grants for job design, training subsidies and wage offsets, we need to expand its reach.

sections.label: Funding for micro-enterprise job redesign
sections.summary: The passage recommends raising job-redesign funding for micro-enterprises to 95% with a higher cap, plus rent subsidies and a facilitator team.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To do this, I recommend that the job-redesign funding for micro-enterprises running mom and pop shops be increased to 95% with a higher cap, provide rent subsidies and a dedicated facilitator team to help shop owners in this particular effort.

sections.label: MRSS grant for PwDs under 55
sections.summary: Eligible PwDs below 55 receive the MRSS matching grant on CPF Special Account cash top-ups, gaining higher CPF savings and payouts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: Eligible PwDs below the age of 55 will receive the MRSS matching grant on cash top-ups to their Central Provident Fund (CPF) Special Account and benefit from higher CPF savings and monthly payouts in retirement.

sections.label: MSF inclusive employment policies
sections.summary: MSF and SG Enable address these issues through inclusive employment policies, vocational training and business support for accommodations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: MSF and SG Enable have been working hard to address these issues through policies that encourage inclusive employment, vocational training programmes and support for businesses to make accommodations.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan 2030 progress update
sections.summary: The passage asks MSF for an update on Enabling Masterplan 2030 progress and plans for adult PwDs and caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can MSF provide an update on the progress of our Enabling Masterplan 2030?

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: With regard to the post-18 cliff, living options, employment and caregiving arrangements are prime concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: What are our plans to further alleviate concerns that adult PwDs and their caregivers have?

sections.label: SSA employee mental health survey
sections.summary: A survey of 88 SSA employees found dissatisfaction, stress, anxiety, depression and discomfort discussing mental health with HR.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: In a recent survey my team and I conducted, which 88 SSA employees responded to, half were dissatisfied with work-life balance, 24% reported high stress and anxiety and almost 20% experienced emotional exhaustion and even depression and mental health challenges since joining the sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: A staggering 68.2% indicated they experienced symptoms of anxiety and depression specifically.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: About 57% of respondents did not feel comfortable discussing their mental health challenges with their HR.

sections.label: Culture pulse checks for SSAs
sections.summary: The passage urges the National Council of Social Service to implement organisational culture pulse checks every three years for all SSAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: One, I urge the National Council of Social Service to implement organisational culture pulse checks every three years for all SSAs.

sections.label: Attracting and retaining social service talent
sections.summary: The passage asks how the social service sector can attract, nurture and retain talent beyond wages, including volunteers and retrained workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Steps have been in place for many years to uplift pay scales with Government support as many service providers are charities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In labour-tight Singapore, how might the social service sector continue to attract, nurture and retain talent beyond just better wages?

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the Minister consider actively building a pool of trained volunteers in key areas of need to complement the full-time professional teams?

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we see jobs in some commercial sectors reduce, can we actively retrain displaced workers to take up jobs in the social service sector?
